name: Haldensee
kurzbeschreibung: Haldensee at 1,124 m in the Tannheimer Tal: crystal-clear mountain and bathing lake between Grän and Nesselwängle featuring the Wasserwelt Haldensee recreation centre.
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque Haldensee is situated at an altitude of 1,124 metres in the heart of the Tyrolean Tannheimer Tal – one of Europe's most enchanting high valleys in the district of Reutte (Außerfern). Nestled between the traditional mountain communities of Grän and Nesselwängle, this crystal-clear body of water extends across roughly 73 hectares and reaches depths of up to 22 metres. Framed by the bold limestone peaks of the Tannheimer mountains – including the world-famous climbing summits Rote Flüh, Gimpel, and Krinnenspitze –, Haldensee harmoniously combines pristine alpine nature with top-tier recreational opportunities for swimmers, water sports enthusiasts, and leisure walkers.

Nature, Water Quality & Leisure Experience

Haldensee was formed during the last ice age, when powerful glacial scouring carved out the natural high basin. Fed by clean mountain streams, the lake is distinguished by first-class Class I water quality. Thanks to its sunny location on the plateau, the surface water warms in high summer (July and August) to a pleasant 20 to 24 °C, making Haldensee one of western Austria's most popular bathing lakes. On the western shore in Grän lies the modern leisure facility Wasserwelt Haldensee: a family-friendly outdoor and lido complex boasting a solar-heated open-air pool, a 50-metre water slide, toddlers' splash area, expansive sunbathing lawns, and direct access to the natural bathing lake. Active visitors can hire rowing boats, pedal boats, and stand-up paddleboards (SUP); windsurfing and sailing are also permitted on the lake. For walkers and nature enthusiasts, the roughly 5-kilometre Haldensee-Rundweg leads completely around the lake: this virtually flat shoreline promenade passes protected reed beds and flowering wet meadows, offering breathtaking photographic angles of the craggy peaks. In winter, the lake becomes a haven for winter sports enthusiasts, featuring groomed cross-country ski tracks and ice skating opportunities.

Visit & Getting There

The shoreline path and the free public lawn areas on the eastern shore are accessible year-round and free of charge. In swimming weather, the open-air bath Wasserwelt Haldensee is open daily from late May to early September from 09:00 to 18:30. Admission prices for Wasserwelt (2025/2026 season): adult day ticket approx. €7.50 (approx. €6.50 with the local Tannheimer Tal guest card), children approx. €4.00, family tickets from €18.00. Arrival by car: from the north toll-free via Füssen or Pfronten (Germany) into the Tannheimer Tal on the B199 to Haldensee/Grän; from the south/Tyrol via the Inntalautobahn A12 to Imst/Reutte and over the Fernpass (B179) to Weißenbach and up into the valley on the B199. Large paid car parks are available right by the Wasserwelt and at the eastern shore. By public transport: train to Sonthofen (Bavaria) or Reutte in Tirol station, from where VVT bus line 120 runs at frequent intervals directly to the stop Haldensee Seestraße.

Tips

The five-kilometre lakeside circular trail is almost entirely paved or finely gravelled, making it exceptionally accessible for wheelchair users, seniors, and families with pushchairs. Following your circuit around the lake, the lakeside restaurant with sun terrace on the western shore invites you to enjoy freshly caught Tyrolean lake trout and homemade cakes. At sunrise, the Rote Flüh reflects spectacularly in the calm water – an absolute insider tip for landscape photographers.
